taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, the US East Coast will be on Daylight Saving Time (EDT), which is 4 hours behind UTC. Madrid will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is 2 hours ahead of UTC. This makes Madrid 6 hours ahead of the contest's deadline time. Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) gives 11:00 PM (23:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru, uses Peru Time (PET), which is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC-5). To find your local deadline, you need to subtract 5 hours from the UTC time.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is 2 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC+2). Your local time in Tokyo is Japan Standard Time (JST), which is 9 hours ahead of UTC (UTC+9). This means Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of the CEST zone. Therefore, to find the deadline in your local time, you add 7 hours to 9:00 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 11, 2026, Madrid will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. The deadline is in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of the contest's time zone. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM on October 11 will place the deadline on the morning of the next day for you.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Of course. Let's determine the deadline in your local time.

The deadline is 11:59 PM on October 28, 2026, in Pacific Time (PT). On that date, the US will still be on Daylight Saving Time, so the specific timezone is Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7.

In late October 2026, Spain will have already switched back to standard time. Madrid's timezone will be Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1. This means Madrid is 8 hours ahead of the deadline's timezone (PDT).

Therefore, we need to add 8 hours to October 28, 11:59 PM, which pushes the deadline into the next morning for you.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is 1 hour ahead of UTC (UTC+1). On that date, the US East Coast will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is 4 hours behind UTC (UTC-4). This means Madrid is 5 hours ahead of the event time. Therefore, 9:00 AM ET will be 2:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 27, 2026, New York will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. On that same date, Central European Time (CET) will be UTC+1, as European summer time will have just ended. This means your local time is 5 hours behind CET. Therefore, 18:00 CET is 13:00 in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in your local time, we need to compare Madrid's time zone with Pacific Time (PT).

On November 2, 2026, the US will have returned to standard time, so "PT" will be Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is 8 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC-8). On that same date, Spain will also be on its standard time, Central European Time (CET), which is 1 hour ahead of UTC (UTC+1).

This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM on November 2 pushes the time into the next morning for you.

This makes the deadline 04:00 UTC. Madrid, Spain, will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Therefore, the deadline in your local time is six hours ahead of ET.
